newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Russia economy to grow 3 pct in '97 - EBRD.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Russia economy to grow 3 pct in '97 - EBRD.

text.p: Russia, the giant of the old East Bloc, which it has mostly lagged in the transition to capitalism, should finally see its economy grow in 1997, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Monday.
In its annual transition report on eastern Europe, the EBRD predicted that Russian gross domestic product would grow three percent next year compared to minus three percent in 1996.
The economy has fallen every year since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, with production showing huge rates of decline.

"Industrial production is beginning to show increases...We are more optimistic about growth returning because output isn't going to decline forever," senior EBRD economist Kasper Bartholdy told reporters.
The direction of economic change has been positive, with inflation down sharply.

"The level of (domestic) investment, which is now at a very low level...is ready to increase in response partly to much better macroeconomic management, especially a much lower rate of inflation," he said.
"All the uncertainties are still there, but we believe that on balance the signals are in the direction of positive growth next year," Bartholdy added.
